\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رمادي} (ramādī)}{رمادي (ramādī)}]{\ar{رمادي} (ramādī) — grey}

\label{lesson:AR-C179-ramadi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for clear, then the Arabic for hard-working.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رمادي}}
\textbf{\ar{رمادي}} — \emph{ramādī} — \textquotedblleft{}grey\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رمادي}} (\emph{ramādī}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-m-d}, \textquotedblleft{}ashes\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Ramādī} is \emph{ramād}, \textquotedblleft{}ashes\textquotedblright{}, with the adjective ending \emph{-ī}: \textquotedblleft{}ash-coloured\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ramādī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ramādī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ramādī}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for clear, then the Arabic for hard-working, then say \emph{ramādī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{رمادي} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Grey\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
